quest.title: Headlong Into the Sands
quest.description: The appointed time has come. Seek out the truth in the sea of sand.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looking at the map... We should be getting close...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, the closer we get, the more Paimon's heart feels like it's beating out of her chest...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Must just be jitters of excitement.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Excitement... Yeah, sure. That's it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, look! It's Tighnari and the others! Everyone's here bright and early.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They must have set out last night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, the desert's a pretty harsh environment. Better to travel at night and beat the heat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, everyone! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ah, right on time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like the desert's treating you okay so far.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You don't need to worry about me. It's not too hot yet, and I'm properly hydrated.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Alright, we're just waiting on the two people Miss Layla mentioned, and then we'll be set.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about Djer?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: He's staying behind. If we don't make it back after a certain time, he'll be in charge of rescue operations.

dialogues.speaker: Djer
dialogues.text: You can count on me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice. You've thought of everything!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, and Cyrus said he'll be in Aaru Village, so he's also available if we need help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haha, amazing. Having people to watch our back is making Paimon a lot less nervous!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you get a good night's sleep, Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Yeah, I did.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: After hearing about what happened, my advisor gave me some time off to rest, so my studies are on hold for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, does your advisor know you're back in the desert to investigate?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Yes. But, I was only allowed to come after I mentioned the General Mahamatra would be there too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, quite the reputation you've got there, Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, something wrong? You haven't said a word this whole time. Are you in a bad mood or something?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Being skilled with words also means being a good listener. I'm just reflecting on what you're sayi—

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ah! Alhaitham! Kaveh! Ha, over here!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Darn it. I was just setting up a brilliant—

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah. I'm sure you'll find another chance.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: The important thing is, our Scribe and our renowned architect are here at last.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Haha, high praise...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: But, wait, why am I renowned and not him? He's just as famous as Cyno, Dehya, or Nilou...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That just means your level of fame is even greater. How could a lowly Scribe hold a candle to you...?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Lowly scribe? Please. All those strings you pulled to get those new books from the House of Daena... What do you call that?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Borrowing. Anyone with an employee ID can do it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Uh huh, yeah. The House of Daena bends over backwards for just anyone, does it?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Send a report to Lesser Lord Kusanali, then. Let her know someone at the Akademiya is abusing their position.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hey! I never said abusing—

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Haha, impressive verbal sparring, as always...

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop! Beep-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Oh, hello to you too, Mehrak! Well, looks like your assistant is raring to go, Kaveh.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: So, I say we get this show on the road. No sense delaying the inevitable.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: No need. We're in this together, remember?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Djer! This is the entrance, yeah?

response.speaker: Djer
response.text: Yes!

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Perfect! Then, if we're all set, let's get moving.

talks.objective: Proceed deeper into the unknown ruins

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (According to the other Layla, there should be a door nearby with a strange device in front of it... Ah, there it is.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But the door is shut, and the device... seems to be out of energy? In that case, it should be disabled.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Good. At least we won't fall into the same trap. I should probably remind everyone not to touch anything, though.)

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Well, that goes without saying.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Fair point. There's just one problem, though...

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: The only way forward is through that door.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh, is it time to hunt for a key? Paimon loves this part!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, with our adventuring experience, we'll find it no problem! Let's get searching!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pffft! Ugh, Paimon's mouth is full of sand... Ugh! So that's what falling into quicksand feels like...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If this was quicksand, we would have struggled to breathe. No... I think this was regular sand. And we didn't sink into it, we fell through it... into this place.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Agreed.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Hehe, in other words, sounds like a "you" problem, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haha, very funny. No way Paimon's the only one...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Pffft! Blech!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah! See?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Heh.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What? I'm the only one with sand in my shoes? Yeah, right...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This place... looks kind of familiar...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Well, looks like everyone made it here unscathed. Let's keep going.)

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This chamber is huge... I can't even imagine what it's used for...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I seem to have stepped on some kind of... stone slab?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Huh, there's a pattern on this... But, it's hard to make out with all the dust.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hm? Look. The shape seems to match the markings on the ground over there.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Let's slot it in and see.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: And, we have a match. Looks like we need to find the other three broken slabs.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let's search the area. But, be careful where you step.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Mehrak... This isn't really your old home, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, no idea what that means, but Mehrak does sound pretty happy.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So, mechanical life forms do have the capacity to miss home. A novel discovery.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, with Mehrak leading the way, we should be safe, right?

response.speaker: Mehrak
response.text: Beep-boop!

choices.text: I'll open the door. Stay on your guard, everyone.

talks.objective: Use the key to continue forward

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on, at this rate, Paimon's gonna lose her title as best guide to a mechanical suitcase...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Awww, thanks! Hey, wait! What do you mean, "useless"?

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Well, no weird mental symptoms so far... I'll take that as a win.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: That said...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: There are three doors here...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: So... we split up. Divide and conquer. Otherwise... this whole thing is in ruins.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Ah, no pun intended on that last part. I swear.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Yeah, that might be our best option.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Good idea. And, the minute things go south, we go back the way we came.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, this is getting exciting...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, who's teaming up with who?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon calls dibs on {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After a quick discussion, the teams and routes are decided.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Mehrak was a popular pick, but ultimately it's decided that Mehrak should go with... or rather, lead Kaveh's team.

choices.text: But we'll need to mark our paths.
Even at your most useless, you're stuck with me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Looks like we found them all — the pieces fit together like a glove.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: But we can't see what's on them...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Turn around.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Look.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh! I've seen this before. It can create strong winds — just what we need to clean off the slab.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's— Hey!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me. If I sit here, I won't be in the way.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, you don't want to be in the way? Then, sit right in front, so the device can blow you straight back to Sumeru City.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We just need one more...
Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Look! A cat... Could it be the same one Djer mentioned?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I don't think we need to worry about startling him. He doesn't seem afraid of people.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Yeah, if anything, it seems like he wants us to follow.

talks.objective: Follow the cat's guidance to obtain one more stone slab

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Oh, he led us to the last piece. Hehe, who's a good kitty...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I... never thought I'd hear you say something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You've clearly never heard how the Professor talks to his tomatoes, then.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Alright, well that's that. Now, we need to figure out how to get rid of all this dust...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Behold! The Great Vayuvyastra!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: ...Be honest. You've been waiting to say that for... how long now?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Just... activate the mechanism.

talks.objective: Activate the Great Vayuvyastra by attacking it

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Done!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh... That's one big cat.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: And there's a shattered crown... I think it's depicting some kind of story.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Look, there's writing too.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "...The Ibis King answered the young noble... granting him the wisdom he sought..."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "...But the fragile crown was shattered by lies in the end..."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "...Here I leave the name... Goudarz."

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Goudarz? I've seen that name in a history book before...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: He was a young noble who sought to save his realm, and a king who once united the desert...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's right. Although, his methods were rather shameful.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: During his long reign, he betrayed his family and the nobles who supported him, only realizing the error of his ways after his enemies left him nowhere to turn.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: But by then, it was too late.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Seems like a common occurrence across history...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Different people, same mistakes — it's an inevitable pattern, destined to repeat itself.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: The writing mentions "the Ibis King," but a cat is depicted here. Does that mean...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So far, what's depicted on the slab seems true to history.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In which case, this cat is either a proxy for the Ibis King or a manifestation of said King himself.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Exaggeration is a common method ancient records use to highlight a being of higher status.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: And, as we know, Layla and Djer both heard the sound of a cat while escaping the ruin.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You're saying, the Ibis King, one of the legendary Seven Pillars of King Deshret, is here, still helping those in need?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm saying, we can't rule it out... Hmm?
Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Wait, there it is! The cat!

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ah! Mehrak went after him!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The cat's showing us the way forward. Come, let's follow.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Okay!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Huh, it worked!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: It's a picture of...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Three Hermanubises?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That can't be right. The ears aren't vertical.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Oh, true. And the looks fall short. My hat is much better-looking.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: A goat, an ibis, and a crocodile...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Oh, wow. Our botanist knows more than just plants.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Riveting observation.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I was just thinking... These three figures look a lot like the Seven Pillars of King Deshret.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: That's right. These are our colleagues.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Our what now?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You sure about that?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Haha, just kidding. What I meant by that is, these were Hermanubis' colleagues back then.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: The middle one is the Goat King Heryshaf, Minister of Ministers, the god Amun's most trusted chancellor.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Records say he was the deputy king of the desert sands, chief among the Seven Pillars.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Someone even more impressive than Hermanubis... I wonder if that ever "got his goat."

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sorry, couldn't resist.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Pfft.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ahem... Okay... that was a good one.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Wait, really? I've got so much more where that came from...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Ahem! Where were we?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: This is Sobek the Crocodile King, Captain of Captains. As the name suggests, he was a valiant commander, and had dominion over all weapons of war.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: And finally, this is the Ibis King Thoth, Scribe of Scribes.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Your memory's pretty impressive. I bet you're almost as good as me at memorizing cards.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: A scribe... Did he manage archives, then? Like Alhaitham?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Wait, that's all Alhaitham does? I never knew being an Akademiya Scribe was such a cushy job...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, that's how his... friend put it, anyway. But, it does seem like he has a lot of free time.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Well, I don't know much about the Akademiya, but I'm sure the Ibis King had more responsibilities than that.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: The Temple's records say he represented the wisest aspects of King Deshret, inventing the desert script and arcane arts at his king's command.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: He must have been quite the impressive man, then.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Or creature, depending on how you look at it.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Still, why are these three the only ones represented here? What about the other Pillars of King Deshret?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Maybe because... the three of them were extra close?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Huh, kinda like us.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah! Maybe we should have someone inscribe us on a commemorative stone slab, too.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Or... we could just take a picture. It would serve the same purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Anyway, no more distractions. Huh... Doesn't it look like there's writing carved into the corner?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Huh, there is... and it's in the ancient desert script, too.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Looks like the Ibis King left you some homework.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Gimme a sec. I'll try and translate it.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: "...The ministers are unvirtuous, the scribes unwise, the captains unworthy..."

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: "...My end is not humanity's end..."

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: "...Hereby bestow upon you all... the far side o{RUBY#[D]Aaru}f Eternity..."

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Wait, so... They went to Aaru?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It doesn't sound like it was their idea...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: The far side of Eternity... is said to be the final land of dreams for all desert dwellers. But if such a place did exist, wouldn't it also be an inescapable prison?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, and based on the writing here, it's clear King Deshret wasn't pleased with these three.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This "gift" he bestowed upon them... seems more like a punishment. Such is the power of a king, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Which means, the goat's the one who got "got" in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Huh... Yep. Not as good the second time.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: W—What!? I—Impossible!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Well, looks like that's all we can learn here. Should we keep going?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes. No time to waste.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, now let's take a look...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Seems like the notes of someone who was trapped here.)

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Maybe this person fell in by accident, like Mr. Djer and me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, maybe. But, they don't sound super worried about their situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So, either this person's an ace adventurer like {NICKNAME}, or some kind of... super optimist!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: An "optimist," huh... I wish I could be that sort of person...

choices.text: Well, blind optimism isn't good, either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! You're detailed and passionate — great qualities for an adventuring buddy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This "optimist" seems super obsessed with exploring every corner of this place... That could've gotten them in big trouble, for all we know!

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Hehe... Well, I appreciate the compliment.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: It's almost magical how words like that can make you feel like... you can do anything...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: I only wish that magic could last a little longer... until I figure out my new study topic, at least...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's keep reading.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Oh, looks like you were spot on, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See, told ya! That's what happens when you don't think things through!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And all this talk about seniors and juniors... He was a student just like you, Layla!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He sure talks a big talk for a student, though. You'd think he was some kind of old scholar instead...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it? Did Paimon say something wrong?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: No, not at all.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: I was just thinking, and this might sound rude, but the way this person speaks is just so...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Cold?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: You noticed too!

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: I mean, it's good that he helped treat his companion's wound, but it didn't seem like it was out of kindness. More like, he was looking out for his own self-interest... or thought he could get something out of it.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: I don't know... Maybe I'm reading too much into it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you're both in this dangerous situation together, wouldn't you mention them at least once?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If it were Paimon, she would write down the name of every single person she was with! No one would be able to get away!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, you'd all be stuck there together, so...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Actually, I find Paimon's approach quite sensible. It makes sense from a safety perspective too.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: That way, if anyone came to the rescue, the notes would be able to tell them everything they needed to know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that's genius-level thinking!

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: O—Oh... Well, I learned that from Madam Faruzan, actually. I'm not speaking from personal experience or anything...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Oh, no, no. I—I'm just a student!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's fine! You taught us something, so you're our teacher! Simple as that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, from the looks of things, the student who left these notes behind was pretty weird... Let's keep reading.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, hang on. That's a lot of information. Paimon needs a moment to take this in...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Ibis King... So, did this person actually meet the Ibis King here?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nefer talked about the Ibis King before...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: S—Sorry, who?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh, you've never heard of the Ibis King? Strange...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Geez, not again. Stop teasing her, Traveler! You know she was asking about Nefer!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, Nefer's, um... a friend of ours, and she's mentioned the Ibis King before, but not in much detail...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh, Paimon handled that pretty well, actually. She managed not to spill any of Nefer's secrets.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Guess the boss of the Curatorium has earned her respect and then some.)

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Oh, I see.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Well, that's not too surprising. Most people in Sumeru know about King Deshret, and most in the Akademiya have at least some knowledge on the Seven Pillars.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Legend has it, King Deshret ruled the desert at the head of several wise retainers, guiding their people to pursue the limits of wisdom.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: He also left behind treasures for future generations, which continue to be relevant in nearly every research discipline.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Now, this message indicates this student and his senior were rescued by the Ibis King.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: But to think it's possible to meet him in a place like this...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: We don't know when these notes were written, but didn't the Seven Pillars disappear a long time ago...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, the notes made it sound like his powers were restricted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, the mention of "this form"... What is that supposed to mean...?

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: I'm not sure... Let's keep reading.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, this is the last page. There's even a signature at the end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, sounds like they made it out! Guess it was a happy ending, after all!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I hope so...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Wait, but it says, "The Ibis King cannot be trusted"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, our friend said something similar... that the Ibis King was a liar...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And the notes did make it seem like something wasn't quite right with him...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! Maybe he wasn't one of the Seven Pillars at all, but some kind of... con-artist!

choices.text: A thousand apologies, eminent lord. Paimon meant no offense...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek! G—Great Ibis King! If you heard that, Paimon didn't mean it! Please forgive her! Don't trap us here...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: I think Paimon raises a good point. Let's keep our guard up just in case.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Alright, I think that's all the clues around here. How about we—

response.speaker: Mehrak
response.text: Beep-boop?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it's Mehrak! That means Kaveh and the others should be around here, right?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Hello? Anyone up there? Can you hear us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we can!

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: You know, sound travels just fine in an empty chamber like this. You don't have to shout...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Of course, if you're shouting to express your excitement at being reunited, by all means... pretend I never said anything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yelling like this is kinda exhausting. C'mon, let's head back down.

choices.text: Paimon's words do not reflect the opinion of the group.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's that supposed to mean?

choices.text: He didn't even mention this companion on the previous page.
Besides, you have your own strengths, Layla.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, Mehrak stopped.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What is it? Found something?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hmm... Looks like something covered in sand.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Let's get it out, then. C'mon...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, it's a stone slab! Good job, Mehrak!

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Bee-bee-bee-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh... Looks like this part of the picture goes... over there?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In that case, there must be other pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Alright, then let's look arou— Hey! Why are you sitting down?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Hmm? I thought Mehrak was helping.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, so you do know what that word means? Great. Are we supposed to just sit back while Mehrak does all the work?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: No, I doubt you could do that.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: But I can.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You... I...

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: See?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ugh, it's all coming back to me... How insufferable it is to work with this no-good, do-nothing—

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: We could be more efficient, I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'll work on this piece. You take care of the rest.

talks.objective: Split up and search for the stone slabs
Split up and search for the stone slabs
Split up and search for the stone slabs
Attack the mechanism to clear away the dust

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Come then! This way.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Wow, what a tall ceiling...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but for such a big place, it's so... empty. Like no one ever lived here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure must've been boring to live in ancient times, staring at ceilings all day.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Now that you mention it, I've heard some people used to draw star maps on their vaulted ceilings.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Some would even make them transparent to better observe the movement of the stars.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: It sounds so nice... stargazing from the comfort of your own home...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Wait a second. I think I... see something up there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Go check it out for us, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How is Paimon supposed to do that...? Oh, right! Flying... duh.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Sit tight, everyone. Adventurer Paimon will be right back...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, there's nothing super special up there. Just a couple of shelves, tables, jars, and scrolls...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And a whole bunch of dust, dirt, and sand... You really wanna search through all that stuff?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, when you put it that way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon then, let's see what we've got! Paimon's hoping for something super valuable!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's a little high-up, so be careful.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Thanks! I'll stick close.

choices.text: The more dirt, the better the treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh, the cat's... gone.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Yes, but look where he led us.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ohhh...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Another slab... It looks similar to the last one.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, by all means. Take your sweet time. Wouldn't want you to overexert yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh, the scene depicted here...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: ...Seems to be a different tale.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "The Ibis King answered the Jinn-blooded dancing girl... granting her the wisdom she sought..."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "...But enemies plotted to kill her close kin... Snake venom was her self-chosen end..."

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: "...Here I leave the name... Makhaira."

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: The "Temptress of Woe"?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You've heard of her?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Of course. I don't just sit around doodling all day. She's mentioned in tons of papers about the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: As I recall, she was given as a gift to the tyrant king of Gurabad, and later seized the opportunity to kill him.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: After getting her vengeance, she reigned as queen for many years... until her enemies attempted a coup, and she took her own life.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's more or less the version I've read as well. It seems this queen also had dealings with the Ibis King.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'm starting to find this whole "granting wisdom" business a bit concerning. I mean, considering how Goudarz and Makhaira ended up, it might not have been a good thing.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: But, at the same time, if the cat guiding us is linked to the Ibis King, then he doesn't seem like a villain either...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: People are complicated, and the same is true of the servants of the gods, no matter their wisdom or power.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Let's reserve judgment for now and keep moving.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon meant to ask earlier, have your memories come back, Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: No, sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: To be honest, nothing about this experience feels familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Besides, my focus is the stars, so I don't spend a lot of time exploring ancient ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess that makes us the senior researchers in this scenario! Stick close, alright, Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: O—Okay!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I think that's everything. Most of the documents are in the ancient desert script, except these ones...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: These seem old as well, but the handwriting makes them stand out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And there are dates on them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! Let's arrange them in chronological order before we read through.

talks.objective: Sort through the Ragged Notes in your Inventory

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Wow, we all ended up in the same place, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Yeah, what a coincidence!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Indeed. Or as I like to call it... the Chai factor.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Huh? Um, ahem... No reply?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari & Sethos
dialogues.text: Just say it...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Because it's spice to sweet brew again.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Oh, hey! That's a new version!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Wait, what? You've never heard that one?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What are you looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: A place to sit and read my book.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, great! What else is new?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, looks like everyone made it through unscathed.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let's take this chance to get some water, rest a bit, and discuss what we learned. Sound good?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yeah. Let's debrief.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone shares water, food, and also their findings.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: It turns out, Cyno actually did bring some spiced tea.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Welcome to my humble abode.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Your house sure is... spacious, Lord Ibis King.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Haha, I fear it's not quite what it used to be.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: In fact, it has long ceased to be my home at all. It belongs to the descendants of the cats I once raised.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Such adorable creatures, aren't they? Take the one I'm "borrowing" here, for instance. A chubby fellow, with such lovely fur...

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Ahem! Anyway... Tradition dictates that a special guest such as yourself be presented with a gift.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Alas, it's a first come, first served basis, you see. I fear, with the passage of time, none are left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? So the treasure's gone already?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Hah! "Treasure," you say? Hm, not an inaccurate description.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Yes... and no.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I have the power to grant gifts inaccessible to the masses. The only requirement is answering a question... Not a bad deal, yes?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Of course, my questions were given unto me by King Deshret, who in turn received them from the Mistress of Flowers. There are three, and no more.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: What causes our rise and fall?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: What obliterates love and hate?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: What determines truth and falsehood?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The more he talks, the less Paimon understands...

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: I see... That must mean Goudarz and Makhaira managed to answer two of the three.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Haha! Another who understands!

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Oh! So that's the event those two slabs are depicting!

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Ah, priests and their records... A singular obsession, and quite boring too...

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: After being imprisoned within Aaru, I could, on occasion, take the form of a cat to converse with those around me, but I despised speaking to them.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: No conversational skills whatsoever!

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Now, humans like you, who stumble in here from time to time... You are much more interesting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on, we're getting off-topic again...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The three questions you just mentioned — what are they for, exactly?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Ah, that is a story that begins with King Deshret...

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: And we're in for another long one...

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Nostalgia for the past is common to us all, is it not?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: And our king... He was such a proud, solemn man in those days...

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: He watched us speak of the present and the future, of the wisdom we possessed or were about to obtain.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: We were his proud retainers, confident in our belief that, so long as each one of us used our abilities to the fullest, progress was inevitable.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Yet, King Deshret's ambition was not destined to be allowed in a closed-off world such as this, so nothing went as planned.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: In fact, from the beginning, there were signs an outcome of this nature was inevitable. Because, although there were Seven Pillars, one was forever absent.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Al-Ahmar would insist the Dendro Dragon Sovereign was one of us, but the dragon herself rejected that idea.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Huh, like a card you can never seem to draw from your deck.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: More like a card that was never in the deck to begin with.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Alas, that's just who Al-Ahmar was. There was nothing we could do about that.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: And I always preferred chess to cards.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: In the end, life grew unbearable for our king. But, of course, those who remain must continue to live on.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: But, subjects like us were less fortunate. After all, the fate of a retainer is decided by the king, including the chance to walk away.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: So it was, then, that King Deshret had Croco, Goatie, and I locked up within Aaru, where we remain to this day.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Croco...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Uhhh... Goatie...?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Ah, of course. You're more familiar with their full names — Sobek, the Crocodile King and Heryshaf, the Goat King.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Hehehe, and let me tell you... When it comes to chess, Heryshaf was a habitual back-seat strategist, always spewing nonsense from the sidelines. While Sobek was all too quick to take his terrible advice, to the point where I was the one who got accused of cheating.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Chess is an exercise in patience, and that man couldn't sit still to save his life. He could never excel at that game.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: In fact, neither of them were good at chess. Even so, we played together often. And, since I was always the winner, we got along quite well.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: ...Hm? What are you laughing at? Were we not good friends?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... No one's laughing... Paimon would never!

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: No, not you. It's Goatie. He's laughing for no reason again. Can you not hear him?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Ah, right. Of course you can't. The two of them are inside Aaru, as am I, so only I can hear them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is even going on here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Has he, like, started to lose it after being trapped for so long?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: That does happen to prisoners serving life sentences.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Speaking of which, how's Azar doing these days?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I doubt he's "doing" much of anything.

response.speaker: Sethos
response.text: Just what I wanted to hear.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: What is the meaning of this? You doubt my words? Hmph, I have half a mind to not talk at all!

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Oh, no. They're not questioning you, Lord Ibis King, just discussing other things. Please, continue.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Hmm. In that case... Where were we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, getting to the part about the three questions, hopefully...?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Ah, yes! We're almost there.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Before I entered Aaru, King Deshret said I could be released from my eternal seal, if I chose humans who could provide the correct answers to those three questions.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: The first person who caught my eye was Goudarz.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I asked him, "what causes our rise and fall?" He answered, "conspiracy and betrayal, for it renders the righteous and wise unable to succeed, and thus nations fall."

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I found his answer quite interesting, so I bestowed upon him the power to "deceive."

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: The second human I chose was Makhaira.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I asked her, "what obliterates love and hate?" She said unto me, "I have nothing left to lose. Vengeance alone can quench both love and hate."

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I found this to be another fascinating response, so I granted her the power to "be loved."

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: But both of them ended up...

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Hehe... Now then, young one, riddle me this. Did their answers point to this fate, or was it the power I bestowed upon them that determined their end?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: I'm just an observer who doesn't understand their circumstances, so I can't answer.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: A clever reply.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I do not wish to comment, either. It is all in the past at this point.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: My only wish was for their answers to be acknowledged by King Deshret's rules, and bring me one step closer to freedom.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: As for the final person... Her fate remains to be seen. So, I will not reveal her name.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That must've been Nefer, then...)

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I asked her, "what determines truth and falsehood?" and found her answer quite compelling, so I bestowed upon her a gift to match.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: As you can see, however, I have not been freed, so it's clear... the answer she gave at that time was wrong.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: But, alas. Three people were chosen, and three questions were asked, so now all I can do is wait.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Wait until her wisdom is in line with the rules set forth by my King... until she has found the true answer to that question.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: No wonder there was no third stone slab, then.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Or perhaps, you're just not ready to include her in the story, though that might be a generous interpretation.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Well, it's not merely because her story remains unfinished.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: As the remaining priests of this place left or passed on, there were none left to record the events that followed.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Besides, stone slabs are few and far between in the Great Red Sands. In the sprawling desert, very few things, or people, even manage to leave a trace.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: But, sometimes, I can't help but wonder...

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: If that young man from several centuries ago had been willing to answer my question, would I have left Aaru by now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so there was someone else?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Of course. It has been thousands of years, after all. All sorts of people have stumbled upon this place, but I only chose the "special" ones.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: That young man had such a singular intelligence, though his companion, by contrast, was rather average.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait. Could that have been...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: The author of those notes we found? The student named Zandik?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Ah... Yes, I think that was his name.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: In truth, I was unsure whether I should grant him my third remaining gift.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: He was, of course, exceedingly clever, but he was also mistrustful and narcissistic in equal measure, and there did not seem to be a line he was unwilling to cross.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Too much power could be dangerous in the hands of someone like him, so I found myself rather relieved when he declined my gift.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Oh, he turned you down? Did he give a reason?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: He said he "didn't need it."

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I still remember the look in his eyes... Nothing stood out, per se, and still... I could sense contempt and disdain radiating from his gaze.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I could not give an exact reason, but on instinct, I just knew... It would not end well to get close to a man like that.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: So, I tricked him.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Stick close to your companion, I said. "Only the descendants of Tulaytullah can come and go as they please. Leave him behind, and there is no escape for you."

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: So, does that mean his companion wasn't a descendant of Tulaytullah?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Oh no, that part was true. The lie was in the other half. Anyone can enter or exit this place — there are no restrictions.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I saw that his companion was exhausted, and was concerned Zandik might leave him behind.. Or worse, that some other "accident" might befall him... So I made up an excuse to prevent Zandik from going a step too far.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Oh, and speaking of, Zandik's companion had the same blue hair and pointed ears as you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, does that mean... Layla's also a descendant of Tulaytullah?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Indeed.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: When Hermanubis founded that city, he took in many who had nowhere else to go. Today, their progeny are scattered to the four winds, and indeed, are far more numerous than I could have imagined.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: So, the person you protected could have been my ancestor...

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Yes, yes. You're very welcome for that.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Could I... ask another question, Lord Ibis King?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Of course. I have nothing but time, I'm afraid.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Did you also save me and a man named Djer?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: I did.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: You two were quite unlucky, bumping into a device King Deshret once used to measure human brain power. That contact caused more knowledge than you could handle to flood into your minds.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: So, I replaced that knowledge with simpler, repetitive information.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Of course, the side-effect being the same thought repeating over and over again in your mind. But, that should resolve itself in time.

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: How many moons are there in the sky?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Yes, that was the phrase I used in your head. I forgot the other one, though I believe it had something to do with food...

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Both were spur of the moment decisions, so no need to dwell on the meaning too much, hehe...

response.speaker: Layla
response.text: Oh, I see... Thank you, Lord Ibis King.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: As I said, young one. You are most welcome.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: If you're inclined to return the favor, perhaps you could turn off that device so no one else can trigger it.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: There's only so much a cat's paw can do, so I'm afraid this is something I must leave to you... or Mehrak, I suppose.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry. That device can no longer be activated.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Oh, splendid! Another one bites the dust!

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Such is the fate of things here. Day by day, little by little, the remnants of ages past fade into obscurity.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: For that reason, the gifts of bygone eras, be they tied to your blood or technological in nature... are not to be revered. They are tools, nothing more.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: ...Disrespectful? Hmph, I simply make the most of what I have. Besides, our King has been gone all these years. What good does it do to revere him now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, are you talking to the Goat King again?

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: No, no. Croco this time.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: He's pestering me for another game of chess. Says he wants to even the score.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Wishful thinking, if you ask me. If we counted one push-up for every loss, he'd owe me three hundred thousand by now.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Of course, that's just a rough estimate. I've never kept count.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It appears that's something you like... being someone unable to be defeated.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Hm, I suppose so...

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Alright, then! Time for me to extend my winning streak, and for you all to head home.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Best of luck to you.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: Hehe...

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: In truth, deep down, I know even the answers to those three questions will not change my fate.

response.speaker: Thoth
response.text: But that is for me to reckon with. Go on now!

choices.text: Are you talking in a literal sense?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: The desert is ever unchanging... I hope it isn't too harsh on the young ones...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Excuse me, do you even know what time it is? I've harvested three crops of tomatoes while you've been gone!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You're exaggerating, Professor.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: I'm making a point! There's a difference!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sincerest apologies for keeping you waiting, Professor Cyrus.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Our mistake. Please accept our apology.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: See? That's what I call manners. Now, are any of you hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope! It went way smoother than we expected, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: I presume the investigation is complete, then? Come, come, tell me all about it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Cyrus what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh my, did you luck out.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: If you've read the work from the Vahumana Darshan, you would know that the Ibis King has... Well, let's call it a mixed record.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Perhaps he's softened up a bit in his old age, and that's why he chose to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Or... Perhaps he just didn't have a good enough reason not to help us.

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: See? Mehrak agrees.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: How do you even know that's what Mehrak meant? That could have just been a happy noise.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: In any case, there's a lot to be happy about! We figured out what happened to Layla and Djer, and there were some unexpected takeaways, too!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Yeah, I never expected to learn about my ancestry...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I've always thought of myself as just an ordinary student. I never would have even considered something like that could be true...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, our ancestors might even have been friends at some point.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Huh, you're right!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Maybe I should take a trip back home to see if I can find any records about that...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, I was just throwing that out there, haha. I wouldn't want you to go to the trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: It's fine. My advisor gave me a break, and I still have a few days left, so...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Oh, wait! My study topic! I haven't made any progress at all! No, no. I need to focus on that instead...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: One thing at a time, Layla.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: R—Right...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Couldn't you help her, Professor?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Eh? N—No, no. I could never—

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Me, you say? I'm from the Spantamad Darshan, and I don't think that Naphis or Zaha Hadi research the stars.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: All I have to offer are my home-grown tomatoes...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Although, I suppose it's not impossible. I can ask a few old friends to recommend some interesting topics.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: You really don't have to! It sounds like a lot of work...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hardly! A few passing questions while we water the plants... It's no trouble at all!

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Of course! Now, it's getting late, and you all must be tired. Let's wrap things up here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Some say desert nights are the sun taking mercy on us after the heat of the day, so let's leave while she still feels merciful.

dialogues.speaker: Djer
dialogues.text: I hope everything goes well in there. I've got your back from out here.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Better get to work. Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Djer
dialogues.text: You made it back safe and sound! Glad to see it!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A little earlier, in a different part of the ruins...

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Mehrak seems interested in these jars. Go smash them.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Well, this takes me back. The last time we were in the desert together, the two of you came all the way out here to gang up on me.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Oh? Sounds like someone's holding a grudge... Just what I like to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If you're still hung up on that last one, just name the time and place, and we'll have ourselves another thrilling...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Umm... Uh... D—Duel... Mm... Ahem...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Huh. What's with the awkward pause? Were you expecting me to stop you from saying something stupid?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You two can have a thousand duels for all I care... after we're done here. For now, focus on the task at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop! Beep-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A little earlier, in a different part of the ruins...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Mehrak! Wait!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Found one!

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-boop!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! There are monsters here? Djer didn't say anything about that...!

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Probably means he didn't run into any. Guess we're just unlucky.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Not the best sign of what's to come...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: It'll be fine. Let's just use up all our bad luck, and we'll be golden.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ah well, we would hate for you to have to lift a finger, your highness...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good thing you decided to join, Kaveh! Otherwise, our investigation would have ended at that door!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It was nothing that I did... You should thank Mehrak instead!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Good teamwork!
